text: NASA says it takes fifty-five times more energy to reach the Sun than to reach Mars.
That sounds backwards. Everything in the solar system is falling around the Sun.
Hold a rock still, one hundred and forty-nine point six million kilometres out, and let go.
By our own sum, it would fall straight in, in about sixty-five days.
And it would arrive at about six hundred and sixteen kilometres every second.
But Parker Solar Probe launched in August 2018 and made its closest pass in December 2024. Over six years, not sixty-five days.
So what makes the Sun so hard to reach? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
